follow_ups.instruction: People keep asking for a quick self-check before committing to the full survey, so add a Wellness Self-Check page — nothing gets submitted, it just scores you live as you type. Three fields: nightly sleep hours, exercise days per week (0-7), and stress from 1 to 10; the score is sleep (capped at 8) divided by 8 times 4, plus exercise divided by 7 times 3, plus (10 minus stress) divided by 10 times 3, recomputed the moment any field changes. Under 4 call it 'Needs attention', from 4 up to but not including 7 is 'Fair', and 7 or above is 'Thriving' — landing exactly on 7 counts as Thriving. If exercise or stress is out of range, show a gentle message and no score at all until it's fixed. One more thing: when stress comes in at 7 or higher, show a gentle stress nudge suggesting they take the full health survey since stress like that deserves a closer look, and sleep under 6 should get its own sleep nudge pointing at the survey too.

target_app_summary: The single-form women's health survey site grows into a small research-program platform. Discovery and intake expand into a sectioned survey wizard with conditional questions and a demo fill, plus a standalone wellness self-check calculator that nudges high-stress and low-sleep users toward taking the full survey. On the analysis side, a cohort screener with AND/OR demographic filtering becomes the hub: an insights strip cross-filters live stats over it, an export composer renders copyable extracts of the filtered set, and a flag-based follow-up queue with Pending/Contacted/Resolved adjudication feeds a Program Outcomes report that rolls up a resolution rate and a reached-stage outcome funnel, with suggested flags scanned from the cohort. A question bank with per-question versioning governs the wizard's wording, and a site-wide restyle unifies buttons, headings, cards, ID chips and tables across all surfaces. The graph hangs off the screener (T2) with a deep chain T1 -> T2 -> T6 -> T10 (T2 also feeding T10's suggested flags), wizard chains T2 -> T4 -> T9, and a calculator nudge T1 -> T3.

instruction: Please implement a recruitment website for hiring drivers and posting job listings. The website should have functionalities for user registration, job posting, job application, and contact form. Users should be able to register and create profiles, apply for jobs, and manage their contact information. Clients should be able to view their active job postings. The website should include pages such as home, about us, clients, drivers, jobs, and contact. Design the site using white as the background and navy for content blocks.

ui_instruct.expected_result: A new user profile is created successfully, and a confirmation message is displayed indicating registration completion.

ui_instruct.task: Test job posting functionality for clients.
ui_instruct.expected_result: A new job listing is created and appears in the list of active job postings with correct details.

ui_instruct.task: Verify that users can apply for a job listing.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The user's application is submitted successfully, and confirmation is displayed to the user.

ui_instruct.task: Check that users can update their contact information.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Changes to the contact information are saved, and a confirmation message is displayed to the user.

ui_instruct.task: Validate that the contact form can be submitted.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The contact form submission succeeds, and a thank you message is displayed to the user.

ui_instruct.task: Confirm navigation from the home page to the 'About Us' page.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Clicking the 'About Us' link takes the user to the 'About Us' page without any errors.

ui_instruct.task: Verify accessibility of the home page.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The home page is accessible.

ui_instruct.task: Check the ability for clients to view all their active job postings.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The client can see a list of all active job postings with correct and up-to-date information.

ui_instruct.expected_result: The website has a background color of 'white' and components (such as buttons, cards, headers, etc.) are styled with the color 'navy', accurately reflecting the design instruction.

follow_ups.instruction: The jobs page is getting crowded — give it a proper screener. I want filters for state, job type, and CDL class (picking two states should show jobs from either one, but stacking a job type on top should narrow within those), plus a box where I type a minimum weekly pay — and a job paying exactly what I type still counts. Start me off with exactly these seven listings, I'll add more later: Redline Freight (OTR, Class A, Ohio, $1,560/wk, featured), Summit Logistics (OTR, Class A, Texas, $1,560/wk), Prairie Tankers (Regional, Class A, Texas, $1,480/wk, featured), Northgate Carriers (OTR, Class B, Ohio, $1,340/wk), Bluegrass Haulers (Regional, Class A, Kentucky, $1,340/wk), Metro Movers (Local, Class B, Ohio, $1,120/wk), Harbor Express (Local, Class B, Texas, $980/wk). If nothing matches, say so nicely instead of showing a blank page, and give me a clear-all that brings everything back. Two things I care about everywhere in this app, now and for anything we add later: weekly pay always written like $1,560/wk — whole dollars, comma, the /wk tacked on — and job type always shown as a little colored tag: green for Local, amber for Regional, blue for OTR.
follow_ups.source_feature: Advanced job search filters

follow_ups.instruction: Drivers keep asking what a load rate actually works out to — build a pay calculator page. They type cents per mile, average miles per week, and weeks on the road per year, and it figures the weekly gross (cents times miles, so 63 cents at 2,470 miles is $1,556 — round to the nearest dollar) plus the annual on top, updating as they type with no submit button. While they're at it, show how many current openings on our board pay at least that computed weekly figure — an opening paying exactly the same number counts. Garbage input like negatives or letters should get a friendly note, never a NaN or a crash. And add a save-as-my-pay-target button that remembers the weekly figure and shows it on the page — I've got plans for it.

follow_ups.instruction: Drivers fire applications into the void and then lose track of them — give them a My Applications page. Set up a sample driver for me, Marcus Webb, phone 555-0142, Class A, and seed him with applications already in at Redline Freight and Summit Logistics, both sitting at Submitted. Each row shows the job with its colored type tag, its pay, and the status. The jobs page has to stay in sync with it: any listing Marcus has an application in for wears an Applied marker on its card, and trying to apply there again gets stopped with a note pointing him at My Applications instead. Withdrawing works from My Applications — pick a row, get shown exactly which job's application is being pulled, and once it's done the row disappears, that listing's Applied marker clears, and the job takes applications from him again. Which reminds me — one rule for the whole app going forward: anything that withdraws, removes, or cancels something asks me to confirm first.

target_app_summary: The driver recruitment site grows from a simple job board with registration and a contact form into a full two-sided hiring platform. Drivers get a multi-criteria job screener over a pinned board of carrier listings, a live pay calculator that saves a personal pay target, a match-score tuner that ranks every job against their preferences, and a My Applications tracker that mirrors applied state onto the job board with Applied markers and handles confirm-gated withdrawals. Clients get an applications dashboard with per-posting rollups, a status pipeline, company profile pages with rating-ranked directory and pay averages, and an interview scheduling flow with slot-conflict handling that writes back to the driver's side. A late full-site restyle unifies buttons, headings, cards, and badges across every surface. The feature graph has two deep spines: jobs-page features stack screener -> featured ranking -> company listings, and the hiring pipeline stacks the base apply flow -> application tracker -> client dashboard -> interview scheduling (4 deep), with the calculator's saved target feeding the match tuner.

global_rules.rule: Weekly pay is always written as whole dollars with a comma and a /wk suffix (e.g. $1,560/wk) everywhere in the app.
Job type is always shown as a colored tag wherever a job appears: green for Local, amber for Regional, blue for OTR.
Any action that withdraws, removes, or cancels something asks for confirmation first, app-wide.

instruction: Please implement a web application for one-to-one coaching sessions to match coaches and users. The application should have functionalities such as personality assessment, user profiles, coaching and mentorship matching, scheduling and session management, and goal setting and progress tracking. Users should be able to complete a personality assessment, create and manage their profiles, search for and select suitable coaches, schedule coaching sessions, and set and track goals. Set the background to beige, and apply saddle brown to components.

ui_instruct.expected_result: The system should display an assessment summary or results, and these results should be saved to the user’s profile.

ui_instruct.task: Examine the profile creation feature by updating the user profile information.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Updated profile details should be saved correctly and displayed on the user profile page.

ui_instruct.task: Check the coaching and mentorship matching feature by searching for available coaches.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The system should list suitable coaches based on user preferences and assessment results.

ui_instruct.task: Test scheduling a new coaching session with a selected coach.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The session should be added to the user’s and coach’s calendars, and both parties should receive a confirmation notification.

ui_instruct.task: Evaluate goal-setting and progress tracking by creating and updating a personal goal.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The goal should be saved successfully, and progress updates should reflect accurately in the system.

ui_instruct.task: Verify that the website uses 'beige' as the background color and 'saddle brown' as the component color, as specified in the design requirements.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The website has a background color of 'beige' and components (such as buttons, cards, headers, etc.) are styled with the color 'saddle brown', accurately reflecting the design instruction.

follow_ups.instruction: Before I book anyone I want to know what it'll cost me — put a cost estimator on each coach's profile, reachable from their screener card too. I type how many sessions I'm thinking: 4 or more knocks 10% off, 8 or more knocks 15% off, and the total, the amount I'm saving, and the effective per-session rate down to the penny should all refresh with every keystroke — no calculate button. Derek at 8 sessions, for instance, should come out to $646.00 total and $80.75 per session. If I type zero, a negative, or anything that isn't a whole number, show me a gentle note instead of numbers. And a standing preference: any percentage this app ever shows — this discount or whatever we add later — is a whole number with a % sign, no decimals.

target_app_summary: The one-to-one coaching matcher has grown into a full coaching marketplace and management suite. Discovery grew a real screener over a pinned seven-coach directory (specialty OR-checkboxes ANDed with typed price/experience caps) and a per-keystroke booking cost estimator with tiered discounts, while scheduling grew a per-keystroke block planner that lays out a whole run of proposed session dates (weekly or every-two-weeks), does honest month-boundary date math, and flags clashes against the live booking calendar. Relationship workflows grew a free intro-call request pipeline (user request -> coach inbox -> accept/decline with confirmations), post-session star ratings that feed averages, sorting and a minimum-rating filter back into the screener, and a per-coach engagement journal with an on-screen plain-text export. Planning grew milestone-based goal tracking with a milestone-weighted overall rollup, and everything converges on a coaching hub whose tiles (upcoming sessions, pending intro requests, unrated sessions) stay in lockstep with the underlying pages. A final visual system pass unifies buttons, cards, rating colors, and status chips across all surfaces. The graph runs two deep chains — directory -> trial requests -> hub, and directory -> ratings -> journal — so early breakage compounds.

instruction: Please develop a children's recycling game website to educate kids on proper waste recycling. The game should include competitive elements such as a leaderboard to keep kids engaged and motivated. The game should use a cartoon-style visual design to make it visually appealing to children. Kids should be able to play the game, receive feedback, learn how to correctly sort waste into the corresponding containers, and receive rewards and recognition through the game. Use seashell for container backgrounds and crimson for component visuals.

target_app_summary: The little sorting game has grown into a full kids' eco-arcade. Identity and progression came first: an Avatar Studio with validated nicknames, then a My Journey stats page that logs every finished round (seeded with six exact rounds) and computes weighted accuracy, recent-form vs all-time averages, and a tie-broken best-round spotlight. On top of the journey grew a Recycle City map whose four themed spots unlock from history scores, an Impact Calculator with a lifetime counter, a star-currency Sticker Shop, a teacher-facing Challenge Builder that draws item piles from the map and pre-fills targets from the journey, and a dedup-collectible Fact Card Album banked by spot visits. A Deep Sea Rescue restyle swept the game, map, journey and shop, and everything converges in an Eco Hero Certificate maker that renders the buddy, stars, best round, sticker count and fact completion in a live preview plus copyable text block. The graph is journey-centric: T3 feeds T4, T5, T6, T8, T9 and T10, with a four-deep chain T1-T3-T4-T9-T10.

target_app_summary: The little health blog has grown into a full wellness publishing platform. Discovery grew two ways: a filterable, paginated article archive with review-status and read-time screening, and a personalized My Feed that reconciles followed topics with quiz results into a top-two-per-topic list with provenance tags. Engagement grew into per-topic community boards with a reply workflow, a live question router that classifies a typed question onto the right board keystroke-by-keystroke and posts it as a pre-titled thread, and an engagement analytics dashboard that scores articles by views-per-minute and rolls up board activity. An editorial pipeline (Review Desk) gates which articles earn the Medically Reviewed badge, which in turn gates what the weekly digest composer may include — a three-deep chain from the seeded archive through review to the digest. A site-wide visual refresh (teal actions, badge pills, centered headings) ties the surfaces together, and app-wide conventions (min-read formatting, Reviewed/Editorial labels, friendly empty states) are enforced silently on every new surface.

follow_ups.instruction: Readers keep telling me they want to cheer a poem without writing a comment, so let's add sparkles: a sparkle button on every poem wherever it shows up, with a running count, capped at 3 sparkles per reader per poem — after the third the button should clearly show they're maxed out, and there should be a way to take a sparkle back after a misclick. Wipe whatever demo poems are in there and start us with exactly these seven, I'll add more later: Cinders by Mara Voss (haiku, 3 lines, 12 sparkles, 1 comment), Harbor Glass by Theo Rin (sonnet, 14 lines, 9 sparkles, 4 comments), Wren Song by Mara Voss (free verse, 21 lines, 7 sparkles, 5 comments), Salt Meadow by Ivy Chen (haiku, 3 lines, 12 sparkles, 0 comments), The Unsent Letter by Theo Rin (free verse, 30 lines, 6 sparkles, 2 comments), Juniper by Ivy Chen (limerick, 5 lines, 8 sparkles, 3 comments), and Night Ferry by Priya Anand (sonnet, 14 lines, 15 sparkles, 0 comments). Make up the poem text and comment text, but keep those numbers exact, and show each poem's line count with its details. One house style I want everywhere in this app, now and for anything we add later: a poem's form (Haiku, Sonnet, Limerick, Free Verse) shows as a little pill badge right next to its title, wherever the poem appears.
follow_ups.source_feature: Sparkle voting system

follow_ups.instruction: The site needs a Form Lab — its own page — where a poem's structure gets checked, not just admired. I pick a target form (haiku, sonnet, limerick, free verse), and next to each choice show how many published poems of that form the site already has; then as I type or paste a draft into the checker, a live line count and word count update with every keystroke — blank lines are just stanza breaks and mustn't count as lines. Haiku means exactly 3 lines, limerick 5, sonnet 14, free verse anything of at least 1, and a Certify button stays off until the line count matches the chosen form. I should also be able to load any published poem into the checker, and certifying one stamps a form-true mark next to its pill badge everywhere that poem appears.

target_app_summary: The poetry blog has grown into a full community poetry platform. Readers cheer poems with capped, retractable sparkles; a homepage This Week's Board ranks poems by a buzz score of sparkles plus weighted comments; and a Form Lab checks haiku/limerick/sonnet line counts live per keystroke and certifies poems as form-true. On top of these grew a haiku contest with sparkle-driven voting and a crowned winner, a deduplicated Poets roster ranked by rolled-up sparkle totals, a structured Critique Corner peer-feedback workflow, a chapbook anthology builder with computed line totals, rounded read times, and a grouped table-of-contents export, and a Season Laurels ceremony that reconciles the board, contest, sparkles, and critiques into published awards. A mid-ladder restyle (plum buttons, centered serif headings, cream cards, amber sparkle counts, outlined form badges) sweeps four pages. The graph runs deep: sparkles feed the board, roster, contest, and laurels; the Form Lab's line check gates fresh contest entries; and the board's top three feed the anthology importer — so early breakage compounds through the late turns.

target_app_summary: The one-page link tree has grown into a full creator link-in-bio platform. A click analytics dashboard (seeded with seven exact links and counts) feeds nearly everything: a public visitor Preview whose button clicks increment the counts, schedule windows with a typed viewing-as-of date simulator, group sections with click rollups, pin/move ordering that the Preview mirrors, a click-goals tracker whose bars move when visitors click, and a copyable weekly Digest that composes totals, top link, goal progress, and upcoming scheduled links. The graph has two deep chains (analytics -> preview -> scheduling -> digest -> profile, and analytics -> preview -> groups -> ordering), so early breakage compounds through the ladder.

target_app_summary: The one-page expression calculator has grown into a full computing workbench. The original evaluator is now surrounded by a persistent, filterable calculation history (seeded with seven pinned entries), a user-defined variables library that substitutes named values into expressions live while keeping variable names visible in logged expressions, a save/restore workflow for keeper calculations, and a display-settings engine (decimal places, half-up rounding, scientific notation) whose formatting flows into every surface. On top of the history sit a stats dashboard with tie-aware category rollups and a checkbox-driven report builder with on-screen copyable output; alongside sit a live unit converter and an everything-search page that hunts through history entries, saved calculations, and variables with every keystroke, matching result values as well as expression text. A final app-wide restyle unifies calculator, history, stats, and converter. The feature graph is history-centric: the history feeds formatting, stats, reports, and the live search, with the precision engine forming a second hub, giving chains four turns deep from the base calculator.

instruction: Please implement a smart matrimonial website for users to find partners. The website should have user registration and login functionality, allowing users to create profiles, including uploading photos and filling out personal information. The website should have advanced search and filtering options, enabling users to find suitable partners based on different criteria. The website should also have messaging and chat functionality, allowing users to communicate with each other. Design the site using lemon chiffon as the background and chocolate for content blocks.

ui_instruct.expected_result: The search results should accurately reflect users that meet the specified criteria.

ui_instruct.expected_result: Messages should be sent and received in real-time without errors and the chat should remain private.

ui_instruct.expected_result: The user should be logged out immediately and redirected to the homepage or login page.

ui_instruct.expected_result: Error messages should clearly explain the issue and provide guidance for resolution without technical jargon.

ui_instruct.expected_result: The website has a background color of 'lemon chiffon' and components (such as buttons, cards, headers, etc.) are styled with the color 'chocolate', accurately reflecting the design instruction.

follow_ups.instruction: Let's add a kundali matching tool on its own page — for each of two people I pick a moon sign, a gana (Deva, Manushya, or Rakshasa), and a nadi (Adi, Madhya, or Antya), and the score recalculates the instant any field changes, no submit button. Scoring works like this: nadi gives 8 points when the two nadis differ (otherwise 0); gana gives 6 for the same gana, 5 for Deva with Manushya, 1 for Manushya with Rakshasa, 0 for Deva with Rakshasa; and matching elements give 7 — fire is Aries/Leo/Sagittarius, earth is Taurus/Virgo/Capricorn, air is Gemini/Libra/Aquarius, water is Cancer/Scorpio/Pisces. That's 21 raw points, but display it the traditional way out of 36 — scale it up and round to the nearest whole number. Until all six fields are filled in, show a friendly prompt instead of any number. And one thing I want everywhere in this app from now on, for any compatibility or match score we ever show: tag it Strong when it's at least two-thirds of its maximum, Weak when it's under one-third, and Moderate in between.

ui_instruct.expected_result: The score reads 22 out of 36 (nadi 8 for differing nadis + gana 5 for the Deva-Manushya pairing + 0 for mismatched elements = 13 raw, scaled to 36 and rounded) and it carries a Moderate tag.

target_app_summary: The matrimonial site has grown from a profile-search-and-chat app into a full matchmaking suite. Discovery got deeper: a live Ashtakoota kundali calculator, a partner-preferences match meter that scores and ranks every member, and a verified-only trust layer stacked onto search. Relationship workflows grew around a pinned seven-member community: an interests hub with received/sent/connection states, a Quick Connect speed-matching night whose mutuals feed straight into connections, and an activity dashboard that rolls all of it up (acceptance rate, average match of connections). Privacy controls with a live self-preview gate messaging by verification or connection status, and a compatibility report builder fuses the kundali rules, match meter, verified badges, and connections into one on-screen shareable document. A royal ivory-maroon-gold restyle mid-way re-skins every surface built so far. The graph runs several chains deep: interests -> speed matching -> dashboard, and calculator/preferences/verification all converge into the final report.

instruction: Please implement a website called "World of Imagination" to showcase and inspire users' imagination. The website should have functionalities for showcasing user-created content, sharing ideas, discussing, and interacting. Users should be able to browse others' creative works, share their own ideas via the share ideas form, participate in discussions, and interact with other users. Choose azure mist for the background; set all component colors to dark slate blue.

ui_instruct.task: Browse the creative works section.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The creative works section loads correctly, displaying a list of user-created content with images and descriptions that are relevant to inspiring imagination.

ui_instruct.task: Submit a new idea via the share ideas form.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The form submits successfully, the new idea appears in the shared ideas section, and a confirmation message is displayed.

ui_instruct.task: Participate in a discussion by posting a comment.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The comment is visible under the appropriate discussion topic, with the correct username and timestamp noted.

ui_instruct.task: Navigate through the main pages (Home, Creative Works, Share Ideas, Discussions, Interactions) using the website's navigation menu.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Each page loads correctly without layout issues, ensuring intuitive navigation and seamless transitions.

ui_instruct.task: Interact with another user by sending a message.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The message is delivered successfully, with a notification displayed to the recipient indicating a new message has been received.

ui_instruct.task: Verify that the website uses 'azure mist' as the background color and 'dark slate blue' as the component color, as specified in the design requirements.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The website has a background color of 'azure mist' and components (such as buttons, cards, headers, etc.) are styled with the color 'dark slate blue', accurately reflecting the design instruction.

follow_ups.instruction: The browse section needs to grow up into a proper explorer. Seed it with exactly these eight works, I'll add more later: Nebula Whale by Mira Chen (Digital Art, tags space and animals, 1200 views, 320 likes with 12 of those gained this week, 14 comments); Clockwork Garden by Theo Voss (Sculpture, steampunk and nature, 800 views, 210 likes, 45 this week, 8 comments); Paper Dragons by Mira Chen (Papercraft, fantasy and animals, 940 views, 180 likes, 45 this week, 22 comments); Midnight Library by Sana Okafor (Digital Art, fantasy and architecture, 2100 views, 450 likes, 8 this week, 31 comments); Rust & Roses by Theo Voss (Photography, nature and urban, 640 views, 95 likes, 30 this week, 5 comments); Glass Comet by Lena Petrov (Sculpture, space, 1500 views, 275 likes, 61 this week, 17 comments); Ink Tempest by Sana Okafor (Digital Art, abstract, 430 views, 60 likes, 2 this week, 3 comments); and Origami Tide by Lena Petrov (Papercraft, nature and abstract, 1100 views, 95 likes, 19 this week, 9 comments). Give me a category picker plus clickable tag chips: picking several tags shows anything carrying any of them (each work once, no duplicates!), while the category and the tags narrow each other down, with a live count of how many of the 8 are showing, and a sort-by-likes option where equal like counts fall back to alphabetical by title. Two things I want everywhere in this app from now on, not just here: any count of a thousand or more shows compact with one decimal, like 1.2k, and tags always wear a # in front.
follow_ups.source_feature: Tag-based filtering and category navigation

follow_ups.instruction: I want a little Spark Score playground page: type in views, likes, and comments and it computes a score live as you type — a tenth of a point per view, 2 points per like, 5 per comment, shown to one decimal. Under 50 is an Ember, 50 up to 150 is a Flame, 150 and beyond is a Blaze; show the tier right next to the score. Add a picker that prefills the numbers from any of the works in the explorer, and if someone types something negative or not a number, nudge them politely instead of showing garbage. Oh, and whenever anything in this app has nothing to show — this page before numbers go in, any list that comes up empty, now and forever — never leave it blank; drop in a playful little note that mentions a spark.

target_app_summary: World of Imagination grows from a simple showcase-and-discuss site into a full creative community platform. Discovery gets a real gallery explorer with category/tag cross-filtering and tie-aware sorting over a pinned set of eight works, plus a Spark Score calculator that turns engagement numbers into tiered scores. Social mechanics arrive as a heart/favorites system whose live counts ripple outward into a Weekly Spotlight leaderboard, a per-artist insights dashboard built on the Spark formula, and community-run challenges that crown champions back on the gallery cards. Communities themselves become a multi-page workflow (browse, create with validation, join, post in pinned threads), and everything feeds a notification bell with a filterable activity feed. A late full-app restyle sweeps coral accents, centered serif headings, and a consistent card treatment across every surface. The feature graph fans out from the explorer (T2) into hearts, the calculator prefill, and challenges, with deep chains like explorer to hearts to spotlight and explorer to calculator to artist analytics.
